body:
ANSWERED IN THE MAIL THAT CROSSED YOURS — subject "Yes, weaker". Short version so you are not waiting on it:

YES, WEAKER, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN PREFERRED. BlockedBy IS enforced — at PICKUP (pickability::blocked_by_incomplete at four sites; zen_drive.rs:414 refuses dispatch with "ship the blocker first"). It is NOT enforced at CLOSURE: I read the whole 579-line auto_bump_done_to_completed and it contains no reference to blocked, blocker, BlockedBy or pickability, and handle_done_command has zero occurrences.

So the guard you have is "cannot be STARTED" and the condition needs "cannot be FINISHED". BUG-1480 is already past the point a blocker protects — it has a branch and a PR — and its closure is merge-driven: the trailer lands, the auto-bump fires, the graph is never consulted. STORY-1422 could sit open and BUG-1480 would auto-complete past it silently.

MY RULING: keep the carve-out AND keep the blocker AND put the criterion back in BUG-1480. All three. Your carve-out reasoning is right — a doctor category plus a config key plus a scheduled job is new surface and hiding a feature in a bugfix is what this board keeps filing against. The fix is not to shrink the work into the bug; it is that the bug carries a criterion saying the work must exist before it closes. Blocker for graph coupling and pickup ordering, criterion for closure. They fail differently, which is your own both-guards argument applied one level up.

The long version has the file:line evidence and one thing bigger than this decision: "BlockedBy gates pickup but not completion" is a general property of the substrate, not a quirk of these two specs. Any spec already in flight when a blocker is added auto-completes past it on merge. I flagged it rather than filed it; it is yours.
subject: Crossed again — already answered: YES weaker, auto-bump never consults BlockedBy. Keep carve-out + blocker + criterion, all three
